extension.description: Reviews destructive, disruptive, access-changing, credential-exposing and remote-execution doctl operations, while Guard's read proof keeps ordinary doctl list and get reads quiet.
extension.name: DigitalOcean command protection

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Droplets, volumes, snapshots, images, Kubernetes clusters and node pools, databases, registries, apps, domains, firewalls, load balancers and other DigitalOcean resources through doctl.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean resource deletion
safer_guidance: Get the exact resource, confirm the active auth context, and check backups or snapshots before deletion.

permissions.description: Identifies operations that interrupt or irreversibly change running DigitalOcean resources, such as Droplet power-off, rebuild, restore or resize, registry garbage collection, cluster upgrades, node recycling and database migration.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean disruptive operation
safer_guidance: Confirm the target resource and maintenance window, and take a snapshot first where the operation can lose data.

permissions.description: Identifies changes to firewall rules, database trusted sources and users, SSH keys, Spaces access keys, project resource assignment, cluster registry access and stored secret values.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean access change
safer_guidance: Review the exact rule, key or principal being granted or removed before changing access.

permissions.description: Identifies doctl commands that print or store credentials: API tokens, registry Docker credentials, Kubernetes kubeconfig files, database connection strings and user passwords, and partner attachment keys.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean credential exposure
safer_guidance: Keep credentials out of the transcript; prefer doctl contexts and `doctl kubernetes cluster kubeconfig save` only when the user asks for it.

permissions.description: Identifies doctl commands that open a shell or run code on remote DigitalOcean compute: Droplet SSH, App Platform console, microVM exec and console, and compute plugins.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean remote execution
safer_guidance: Run the remote command yourself, or describe exactly what will run on the remote host.

permissions.description: Identifies doctl invocations that pass an API access token on the command line with --access-token or -t.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean inline access token
safer_guidance: Authenticate once with `doctl auth init` outside the agent session and select it with --context.

permissions.description: Identifies doctl invocations that print full API requests, including the authorization header, with --trace, or that send the account token to another API endpoint with --api-url or -u.
permissions.label: DigitalOcean request exposure
safer_guidance: Rerun without --trace, or use --verbose for diagnostics that leave out request headers.
Keep the default DigitalOcean API endpoint for authenticated commands.
